name: Brundarok
text: Bronze rail. Carts ride it up to 0.6 blocks per tick, half again vanilla speed. Curves, slopes and junctions work like a normal rail. Age III.

name: Brundavoss
text: Bronze powered rail. Boosts a cart when powered, stops it when not. Caps at 0.6 blocks per tick. Age III.

name: Sorvanquil
text: Steel rail. Carts ride it up to 0.9 blocks per tick, more than twice vanilla speed. Age V.

name: Sorvaleth
text: Steel powered rail. A stronger boost than bronze, same stop when unpowered. Caps at 0.9 blocks per tick. Age V.

name: Zephrakund
text: High-speed rail. Carts ride it up to 1.2 blocks per tick, three times vanilla speed. Keep curves gentle. Age VI.

name: Zephravoss
text: High-speed powered rail. The strongest boost, caps at 1.2 blocks per tick. Age VI.

name: Haldurmek
text: Station rail. Stops a cart that rolls onto it and holds it until the rail is powered, or until its timer ends. Use it bare-handed to cycle the timer: signal only, 2, 5, 15 or 60 seconds. A coupled follower follows its leader instead. Age V.

name: Quelvarith
text: Coupling chain. Use it on one cart, then on a second: the first leads, the second follows at a fixed spacing and is pulled along, so a row of carts runs as a train. A link breaks if the carts get more than 8 blocks apart. Age V.

name: Snithrekel
text: Chain cutters. Sneak and use on a cart to cut its link and get the chain back. Age V.

name: Block Signal
text: Faces a rail and guards the stretch of connected track from there, up to 32 rails each way, round curves and slopes. Red and a redstone signal of 15 while any minecart is on that stretch, green and 0 otherwise. Wire it to a station rail or a powered rail upstream to keep trains apart. Age V.

name: One-Way Rail
text: A rail that lets carts through one way only. The arrow on it points north or east; use it bare-handed to turn it round. A cart that rolls on against the arrow is turned back. Place it on a straight stretch. Age V.

name: Destination Rail
text: Routes carts by name. It gives a redstone signal of 15 while a cart whose name matches its channel stands on it. Use it bare-handed to cycle the channel: any cart, or the letters A to P, matched against the cart name (name a cart "C" with a name tag). Power a three-way junction rail with it and the named carts take the branch. Age V.

name: Cart Loader
text: Stands over a rail with a chest, barrel or tank on top. Every 8 ticks it moves up to 8 items, or 250 mB of fluid, between the container and the cart standing under it: loading from the container, or unloading into it (use it bare-handed to flip). Works on any cart that offers an item or fluid handler, including chest carts, hopper carts and the tank wagons from the yards. Redstone switches it off. Age V.

name: Locking Rail
text: Stops a cart that rolls onto it and keeps it there. Use it bare-handed to change mode. Latch (amber) holds the cart until the rail goes from unpowered to powered, a redstone pulse; a rail already powered when the cart arrived does not release it. Interlock (green) holds the cart until the 32 rails ahead are clear of other carts, then lets it go. Age V.

name: Reaper
text: A steel cutter bar for the edge of a field. Every 2 seconds it cuts every fully grown crop in the strip in front of it (5 wide, 5 deep, at its own height), replants each at the first growth stage, and pushes the harvest into the chest, barrel, hopper or storage port behind it; with no room it spills the harvest on the ground. Use it bare-handed to turn it. Redstone switches it off. Age V.
